crossRefs.note: But he, being merciful, forgave iniquity, and didn’t destroy them. Yes, many times he turned his anger away, and didn’t…
He remembered that they were but flesh, a wind that passes away, and doesn’t come again.
Remember how short my time is, for what vanity you have created all the children of men!
You will eat bread by the sweat of your face until you return to the ground, for you were taken out of it. For you are…
My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.
Why do you not pardon my disobedience, and take away my iniquity? For now will I lie down in the dust. You will seek me…
Remember, I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you bring me into dust again?
Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the dry stubble?
and the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.

translations.web: For he knows how we are made. He remembers that we are dust.
translations.bsb: For He knows our frame; He is mindful that we are dust.
translations.kjv: For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
translations.asv: For he knoweth our frame; He remembereth that we are dust.
